=== PRECONDITIONS RE-VERIFIED FIRST-HAND, NOT TAKEN ON TRUST ===
`git worktree list` shows two entries -- this checkout (C:/Users/tvolo/dev/ai-dala/letflow-2) is the PRIMARY, the secondary (letflow-wt2) sits on fix/ISS-0096-GH324-pack-resolution-enum, and neither held local `main` at dispatch. NON-worktree variant confirmed correct; `git checkout main` at step 9 succeeded, which is the behavioural proof.
`git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD | grep -E '^(lib|test|priv|web|config|mix)'` exits 1 with no output. Docs-and-handoffs only confirmed independently: 7 files under docs/, 10 under handoffs/, nothing else.

=== THE REBASE: origin/main MOVED TWICE, THREE SIBLING SESSIONS, NOT TWO ===
The dispatch anticipated 15 commits from two siblings (7322185 -> 9d277ea, WF03-ISS0201 and WF03-ISS0204). A THIRD landed mid-step: after PR #401 was already open, `gh pr merge` refused with 'the merge commit cannot be cleanly created', and re-fetching showed 9d277ea -> 9930d30, six commits from WF03-ISS0207-20260821 (which extends ISS-0204's own section 1.2). So the branch was rebased TWICE, onto each tip in turn, and the overlap set was re-derived after each rather than carried forward from ORCH's measurement. The overlap held at exactly the three files ORCH named, at both tips -- verified by `comm -12` over the two file lists, not assumed.

=== CONFLICTS, AND HOW EACH WAS RESOLVED ===
HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md never conflicted TEXTUALLY at either rebase -- this run's block inserts at what was line 239 in the base, all three ISS-0201 riders insert above it (base lines 142/188/197) and ISS-0204/0207 insert a whole new section 1.2 above section 2, so git auto-merged. That is precisely the case GIT_MERGE.md warns is easy to miss, so the SEMANTIC check was done anyway and is reported below.
orchestrator.log and registry.json conflicted at BOTH rebases and again at the merge. All were hand-resolved by UNION per ORCHESTRATOR.md 7.1. `--ours`/`--theirs` were not used in either direction: the actual marker content was read each time, and the orientation was CONFIRMED from that content rather than assumed -- during the rebases the HEAD side carried the siblings' lines and the replayed side carried this run's; during the later merge the orientation flipped (HEAD side = this run's), which was observed in the file and the resolution order swapped to match, so the union came out in the same order both ways.
Each resolved file was then RE-READ and compared programmatically rather than claimed from the resolution command:
  - orchestrator.log: 1,021 lines at base 7322185; 1,046 at the first main tip, 1,058 at the second; 1,083 on the branch after resolution, and 1,083 on `main` now. Both sides' lines kept, and origin/main's 1,058 lines are an EXACT PREFIX of the resolved file (list equality over splitlines(), not a count comparison) -- so no sibling line was reordered, re-serialised or dropped. The count grew at every step; it never shrank.
  - registry.json: parses (json.load) after every resolution and on `main` now. 65 runs at base -> 69 now = the three sibling runs plus this one. Every entry present on origin/main compares byte-identical after resolution (json.dumps(sort_keys=True) per entry, all equal), main's entry ORDER is preserved as a prefix, the only resolved-only entry is WF03-ISS0200-20260821, and there are no duplicate run_ids.

=== SEMANTIC CONFLICT CHECK vs ISS-0201's THREE RIDERS AND ISS-0204/0207 -- FINDING: NONE, AND HERE IS WHY FOR EACH ===
Rider 3 ('DROPPING A RESTATEMENT IS HALF THE EDIT', now line 332) imposes an obligation to add a source path to context.artifacts_in when a restatement is dropped. It is a DISPATCH-side obligation about task.description. This run's block ends by declining a RESULT-side row in the same inline-vs-artifacts_in table. Those compose rather than collide: rider 3 makes one side of the table stricter, this block declines to create the other side at all, and the block scopes every sentence to result.summary explicitly. Checked additionally that the block satisfies rider 3 on its own terms -- it cites its source by full relative path (handoffs/WF03-ISS0200-20260821/step-005-01-diagnose.json) inline, so nothing is named by ID with its path absent.
Rider 1 (line 275, 'That count is over the FIELDS of this block', admitting backfill_note as not_agent_attested's optional seventh member) is about the section-2 schema fence's membership. This run's block adds no field to that fence and no member to any object in it, so there is no interaction. Re-verified mechanically: the fence still parses.
Rider 2 (the requirement_text-carries-description-only clarification) constrains what travels under a REQ-ID key. This run is issue-driven, requirement_ids is empty, and the block says nothing about requirement_text. No interaction.
ISS-0204 settled started_at and rewrote section 1 step 3 and section 3's TABLE ROW FOR started_at. This run's block leans on section 4 making the acting agent the only party who may write result.summary -- and section 3's `result` row is untouched by ISS-0204 (read the actual diff hunk; only the started_at row changed), so that premise still holds post-rebase. ISS-0207 further dated and scoped section 1.2's bucket figures with a growth-vs-alarm marker; it concerns started_at gap counts and does not touch result.summary, section 2's tail, or the H-SIZE checks.
Section-number stability was checked too, since a rebase that inserts a whole new subsection could silently invalidate a cross-reference: 1.2 is NEW (inserted between 1 and 2), and 2/3/4/4.1/5 keep their numbers, so every 'section 4' and 'section 2' reference in this run's text still resolves to what it meant.
POSITIONAL check: the block opens by calling itself the counterpart to 'the ISS-0198 dispatch-side finding immediately above'. Post-rebase it is still immediately below that finding, so the sentence is still true rather than merely surviving.

=== ISS-0200 AC4 RE-VERIFIED AFTER THE REBASE, HASHES QUOTED ===
Method reproduced from step-03c/05b rather than invented: extract each span by heading regex, sha256, first 16 hex. It was validated by first re-deriving 03c's figures at 7322185 exactly, before trusting it on anything new.

ONE SCARE, RECORDED BECAUSE IT LOOKS LIKE A VIOLATION AND ISN'T: read from the WORKING TREE, all three spans hashed differently immediately after the first rebase, growing by exactly +73 / +382 / +346 chars -- which is exactly +1 byte per line of each span (73 / 382 / 346 lines). core.autocrlf rewrote the checkout to CRLF when the rebase re-materialised the file. Content-identical: the committed blob normalises to LF, `git status` is clean, and the working copy equals HEAD under CRLF->LF normalisation (verified by explicit comparison). All hashes above are therefore measured against the COMMITTED BLOB, and a future agent re-deriving them should do the same -- 03c measured the working tree, which happened to be LF at that moment and is not guaranteed to be.

=== THE OTHER TWO POST-REBASE CHECKS ===
Section 2's JSON schema fence PARSES (json.loads OK) on main now. Noted for accuracy: section 2 contains five json fences; only the first is a whole document. The four worked-example fences are result-object FRAGMENTS and do not parse standalone -- at 7322185, at origin/main and on main now, identically. That is pre-existing and not something this branch or the rebase introduced; the 'machine-loadable' claim attaches to the schema fence, which is intact.
6,000 is still DECLARED in exactly one place -- the section-2 Enforcement note ('6,000 is a WARN threshold, not a length any dispatch is required to meet', line 1093). The string occurs four times in the file: that declaration, the H-SIZE-1 pseudocode that applies it, and two measurement references. Same four occurrences, same roles, at base / origin/main / main-now -- only line numbers moved. This branch's added text introduces no fifth occurrence and no new numeric threshold.

=== TEST ATTRIBUTION: ROUTE 1 (STRUCTURAL), EVIDENCE IS THE DIFF ===
mix test was NOT run, and that is the correct action rather than an omission. Route 1 per core-directives.md's 'Failure Attribution Is Structural, Never By Count-Matching': the branch's diff contains no module, no test file, no config and no dependency, so there is no causal path by which it could produce a suite failure -- whatever the standing count is. No bare PASS was written next to a non-zero count anywhere; the count is simply not the instrument. Stated in the PR body as well as here, per GIT_MERGE.md step 7's requirement that the attribution appear IN the artefact a human reads. mix compile --warnings-as-errors likewise not run: mix IS available on this host (C:/Program Files/Elixir/bin/mix), so this is a deliberate decision, not a missing toolchain -- compiling here would attest to the state of main, not to this branch, since the rebase touched nothing compilable.

=== PUBLISHING WITHOUT A FORCE-PUSH, AND ORCH'S MID-STEP CORRECTION ===
The first rebase was pushed as a fast-forward (the remote branch was still at 7322185, the branch having been created and pushed empty at Step 00, so 7322185 was an ancestor of the rebased tip). PR #401 was opened from it. The SECOND rebase then rewrote commits already published, which normally forces the choice the dispatch had forbidden.
It was resolved WITHOUT force, and this is the substantive git decision of the step: the branch was reset back to its published tip and origin/main was MERGED into it instead, resolving the same two conflicts by the same union -- then PROVED equivalent rather than assumed so. The merge commit's tree is 6a4a76feaf3c2dee665a7463ce61990815b77ad9, byte-identical to the discarded rebase's tree, and both conflicted files hash-identical between the two routes (git hash-object vs git rev-parse of the rebased tree's path). Since the PR squash-merges, branch topology is erased at merge time and the commit landing on main is identical either way. Every push to the branch was a fast-forward; no force-push of any kind was issued at any point.
ORCH's correction arrived after this was already done: it relaxed 'no force-push under any circumstance' to its intended scope (main and other sessions' commits) and explicitly authorized --force-with-lease on this run's own branch. The correction is recorded verbatim at the end of task.description for the audit trail, per ORCH's instruction. THE AUTHORIZATION WAS NOT EXERCISED -- it was no longer needed, and the route actually taken is strictly weaker in privilege than the one authorized. ORCH's two live-state notes were independently confirmed: origin/main had indeed advanced to 9930d30 (found by this step before the message arrived, via gh's merge refusal), and PR #401 was updated by pushing rather than replaced -- no second PR was opened.

=== ONE SELF-INFLICTED DEFECT, CAUGHT AND FIXED IN-STEP ===
Recorded because a clean-looking log would misrepresent what happened. The commit writing ORCH's correction into task.description (13e3257) left TWO RAW NEWLINES inside the JSON string, breaking json.load on this very handoff file. Caught by validating the file immediately after writing it -- but the validation shared a command with the write while the following `git add` and `git commit` sat on separate lines, so the failed validation did not stop them and the broken file was committed. Fixed in 2098287 by escaping them, and all 8 handoff files in this run plus registry.json were then re-validated as parseable before anything was pushed. The broken state never reached main; it existed for one commit on the feature branch and is squashed out of the merged commit. Cause worth carrying: chaining a write and its validator with newlines instead of `&&` lets a failed validation pass silently into the next command.

issues.description: ORCH's dispatch stated the constraint as 'Do NOT force-push under any circumstance', which ORCH itself corrected mid-step as over-broad. It did not block this step (the same end state was reached by merging, with tree equality proved), but as written it would deadlock any Step Final whose branch is rebased after its first push -- the normal case whenever origin/main moves twice. GIT_MERGE.md step 6 says only 'git push origin feature/<run-id>' and does not address the non-fast-forward that step 5's own rebase guarantees. Worth an issue against GIT_MERGE.md to state the rule at its intended scope (never force main; never force over another session's commits; --force-with-lease on your own branch is the normal republish) and to record the no-force alternative used here: reset to the published tip, merge origin/main, and verify the resulting tree hash equals the rebased tree's.

AC4's byte-identity method is line-ending-sensitive and its provenance says 'the working-tree file'. On this host core.autocrlf rewrites the checkout to CRLF whenever git re-materialises the file, so identical content hashes differently before and after a rebase (+1 byte per line). Step 03c already hit a version of this between its own two runs. Recommend the method be pinned to the COMMITTED BLOB (git show <ref>:<path>) wherever it is cited, so a future re-derivation is stable regardless of checkout state.

Section 2 of HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md contains five json fences, of which only the schema fence is a parseable document; the four worked-example fences are result-object fragments. This is unchanged since 7322185 and is not a defect introduced here, but 'the section-2 JSON fence must still parse' is ambiguous as an acceptance criterion when five fences exist and four are fragments by design. Worth one clause in the AC4 wording naming which fence is meant.

origin/main moved twice during a single Step Final (three sibling sessions merging within roughly one hour), forcing two rebases and one merge-equivalence proof. Not a defect, but this is the second run in a row to hit sibling churn on handoffs/orchestrator.log and handoffs/registry.json, and those two files conflict on essentially every concurrent run. A union merge driver declared in .gitattributes for both paths would make this class of conflict resolve automatically and correctly, since both files are append-only by protocol.
